subject: Clarify: notification windows & evidence routing for potential log exposure (Clearbank)
message_1_subject: Possible log exposure containing customer identifiers
message_1_body:
Hi Ben / Redwood security team,

We found a set of service logs in our ingestion bucket that appear to contain hashed customer IDs and fragments of email addresses for a subset of EU customers (sample attached). The log lines were generated from requests proxied through Redwood on 2027-06-17.

Can you confirm whether Redwood considers this a personal data exposure under our DPA? If so, what timeline can we expect for: 1) initial acknowledgement, 2) an evidence package (redacted if necessary), and 3) forensics cooperation calls? Clearbank needs to decide whether to trigger our regulator notification process.

I've attached a short redacted snippet (log_snippet_0619.txt).

Thanks,
Ellie Summers
Head of Vendor Risk — Clearbank
ellie.summers@clearbank.com

Attachment: log_snippet_0619.txt (text, 3 KB)
message_2_subject: Re: Possible log exposure containing customer identifiers
message_2_body:
Hi Ellie — thanks for flagging and for the sample. Acknowledge receipt. We're treating this as a potential DPA incident until triage proves otherwise.

Immediate actions from Redwood (ops + security):
- Preserve: we will snapshot the implicated logging bucket and mark the object(s) as legal-hold (no deletes) — preservation manifest will follow.
- Triage: infra team will run a quick parse to determine whether the lines contain plaintext PII vs hashed/one-way values and which customer namespaces are affected.
- Subprocessors: we will confirm whether any NimbusCloud or third-party log shippers processed the exact keys observed.
- Communication: propose the following timeline for now — preliminary acknowledgement within 48 hours; a scoped evidence package (redacted) within 5 business days; a full forensic export up to 14 calendar days if cross-border export checks are required.

Notes: I want to be pragmatic — we can tighten the "acknowledge" window to 24 hours if Clearbank needs that for regulator timelines, but the full export may require extra time if we need legal clearance for redaction and cross-border transfer.

I'm looping in Kimberly (legal), Marissa (privacy ops) and Laura (forensics) to confirm the proposed windows and the list of artifacts we'll provide.

Ben Carter
Director, Customer Security Operations
Redwood Inference

-- Forwarded attachment: log_snippet_0619.txt --
message_3_subject: Re: Possible log exposure containing customer identifiers — legal note
message_3_body:
Team — quick legal guidance on timelines and scope under the DPA: 

1) DPA language (Section 6.1) requires us to inform the controller (Clearbank) "without undue delay" and to provide reasonable cooperation. Practically, that translates to an acknowledgement within 48 hours for a confirmed personal data exposure.
2) If the initial triage is inconclusive we should still provide a preliminary notification describing the suspected scope and our investigative steps. That can be the 48-hour acknowledgement Ben proposed.
3) For the evidence package: avoid exporting any raw customer identifiers outside the EU until we confirm lawful transfer mechanisms. A redacted package within 5 business days is acceptable; if we need to involve NimbusCloud or other subprocessors to reconstruct traces, request a 10–14 day window.
4) Preserve chain-of-custody: generate a preservation_manifest.pdf and capture checksums and timestamps. That will be required by Clearbank and by our own audit logs.

I concur with Ben's approach but recommend we commit to a 48-hour preliminary notice in writing to the customer, with a clear caveat that full forensic exports may take longer due to transfer/legal review.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
message_4_subject: Re: Possible log exposure containing customer identifiers — next steps & timeline
message_4_body:
Hi Ellie — following internal triage and legal review, here's the agreed path forward (summary for Clearbank):

1) Acknowledgement: Redwood acknowledges receipt of your report and the snippet. This is your 48-hour preliminary notice.
2) Triage outcome: initial parsing shows a small percentage of lines with partially hashed identifiers and some truncated email fragments; we are treating this as a scope-limited incident at this time.
3) Preservation: we have taken a read-only snapshot and uploaded a preservation manifest. Attachment: preservation_manifest_0619.pdf.
4) Evidence package: we'll provide a redacted evidence bundle (CSV of matched keys with mapping metadata, redaction notes, and checksums) within 5 business days of this message (target: 2027-06-29). If Clearbank requires a full export for regulator review that includes EU raw rows, we will need up to 14 calendar days to complete transfer assessments and any necessary subprocessors' approvals.
5) Cooperation: offer a forensics call on 2027-06-23 at 09:00 UK time to walk through the redacted package and answer questions.

Links and references: PRIV ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PRIV-4573 (we'll attach artifacts there).

If you need us to accelerate the full export timeline to meet a regulator-imposed deadline, please let us know the regulator and target date and we'll escalate to Legal.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Customer Security Operations
Redwood Inference
